lesson.title: Industrialization Spreads in the Period from 1750 to 1900
lesson.summary: How industrialization spread to western Europe, the United States, Russia, and Japan, and how it hurt older manufacturing in places such as India.
learningGoals: Explain how different modes and locations of production developed and changed over time.
Explain how industrialization affected older manufacturing regions.
lesson.bigIdea: Industrialization spread unevenly, making some countries powerful producers while older manufacturing centers such as India's textile industry declined.
lesson.context: Britain tried to keep its machines and methods secret, but skilled workers and plans spread, and other governments and entrepreneurs copied British success.

sections.title: Europe, the United States, and beyond
sections.conceptTitle: Europe, the United States, and beyond

blocks.text: Belgium, France, and the German states began industrializing in the early 1800s. By 1900 Germany and the United States produced more steel than Britain.
Russia and Japan industrialized rapidly in the late 1800s with heavy government involvement. Japan became Asia's leading industrial power.

sections.takeaway: Industrialization spread from Britain, often with government support in late industrializers.

sections.title: Decline of older industries

blocks.text: Machine-made British cloth flooded markets in India, where hand spinners and weavers had supplied much of the world's cotton cloth. India became an exporter of raw cotton instead.
Shifts like this, sometimes called deindustrialization, turned some regions into suppliers of raw materials for industrial countries.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Cheap factory goods undersold handmade cloth, which ruined many artisans and pushed colonies to export raw materials instead.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Industrialization did not make every region richer. It often turned colonies into suppliers of raw materials.

sections.takeaway: Industrial growth in some places caused decline in others.

vocabulary.definition: The decline of manufacturing in a region, such as India's hand-woven textile industry after cheap British cloth arrived.

connections.title: Raw materials and empire
connections.body: Industrial countries needed raw materials and markets, a need that drove the new imperialism studied in Unit 6.
connections.transferQuestion: How might industrialization encourage imperial expansion?
connections.feedback: Explain the link between factories, raw materials, and colonies.

glossary.definition: The decline of manufacturing in a region, such as India's hand-woven textile industry after cheap British cloth arrived.
